title: Derived adic completeness
statement:
Let $E/\Ql$ be finite, with uniformizer $\pi_E$, and let
$\mathcal O_{E,X}=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ and $(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X$ be
the integral and finite coefficient sheaves of
[sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. A complex
$K\in D(X_{\Proet},\mathcal O_E)$ is *derived complete* if its canonical map

$$
K\longrightarrow R\varprojlim_n\bigl(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism. For
$K_n=K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X$, the canonical
transitions satisfy the derived reduction identities
$K_{n+1}\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^{n+1})_X}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X\simeq K_n$;
a compatible tower with these identities is called *normalized*.

Normalization is a property of the complexes $K_n$; their cohomology sheaves
$H^q(K_n)$ need not form a normalized tower under the ordinary tensor product.

proof.text: Unpack the notation with $X$ an arbitrary scheme, $\ell$ prime and $n\geq1$. Put $R=\mathcal O_{E,X}$ and $B_n=(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X$. The valuation ring, uniformizer, quotient rings and quotient homomorphisms are the data of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Apply the continuous-ring construction of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and then the functor on ring objects of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] to obtain compatible maps $R\to B_{n+1}\to B_n$. The ambient category is the unbounded Layer B category $D(\Mod_R)$ of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], applied to the commutative condensed coefficient ring $\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ and its pulled-back ring object $R$. This invokes the ambient-category row, not the constructible subcategory or the general left-derived existence clause of that node; its relative derived tensor is that of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom].

source.place: statement, coefficient sheaves and ambient derived category

proof.text: To use ringed-site lemmas in this Layer B category, take the usual small-site/coefficient-universe convention. The abelian-sheaf tensor is sheafified objectwise $\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$ by [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure] and is closed by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Apply [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] to its commutative ring object $R$. Its equivalence identifies the coequalizer relative tensor with the sectionwise balanced sheaf tensor, preserves exactness and total tensor complexes, and preserves and reflects flatness and K-flatness. Thus all subsequent resolutions, coefficient changes and products concern this same ring sheaf. The comparison required in old step 1 is the statement of this cited lemma; it is no longer an unproved identification inline.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, balanced-bilinear universal property; Tag 0GMW, lemma-sheafification-tensor. Internal-module comparison and passage to total complexes are the extracted agent argument.

proof.text: By [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], choose a K-flat representative $P$ of $K$ whose terms are flat $R$-modules. $P$ is also K-flat in the sense of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]: for a quasi-isomorphism $u:F\to F'$ of $R$-complexes, $\operatorname{Cone}(u)$ is acyclic, and since the tensor preserves direct sums, $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R\operatorname{Cone}(u))\cong\operatorname{Cone}(P\otimes_Ru)$ termwise (with the sign $(-1)^p$ on $P^p\otimes F^{q+1}$), so $P\otimes_Ru$ is a quasi-isomorphism; the symmetry handles $-\otimes_RP$. Hence derived extension of scalars [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars] is computed by this representative, so $P_n=P\otimes_R B_n$ represents $K_n$ as a complex of $B_n$-modules. Restriction of scalars leaves the underlying objects and maps unchanged by clause 1 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Its exactness can be checked directly in the sectionwise-module presentation of step 2: a kernel is the underlying kernel with the restricted action, and a cokernel is the underlying quotient with the induced action. Restricting the ring action therefore preserves both and leaves the exact underlying sequence unchanged. This is the exact restriction used in [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]; no exactness of extension of scalars is asserted. Thus we can regard all $P_n$ as $R$-complexes. The maps $P_{n+1}\to P_n$ send $p\otimes b$ to $p\otimes\bar b$, and the unit maps $c_n:P\to P_n$ send $p$ to $p\otimes1$. They are chain maps and satisfy $t_nc_{n+1}=c_n$ strictly, since both send $p$ to $p\otimes1$. This constructs the reduction cone appearing in the definition.

source.place: Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution; Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change, for identity-topos coefficient change

proof.text: Countable products of $R$-module sheaves are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact], which applies to an arbitrary sheaf of commutative rings and hence to the pulled-back ring $R$. By clause 2 of [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence], the product $Q=\prod_n K_n$ in $D(\Mod_R)$ exists and is represented by $\prod_nP_n$. Let $s:Q\to Q$ have $n$-th component $t_n\operatorname{pr}_{n+1}$. By [def-weil-derived-limit], $R\varprojlim K_n$ means the homotopy limit specified by a distinguished triangle $L\to Q\xrightarrow{1-s}Q\to L[1]$, and it exists by clause 1 of [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence]. On the strict representatives it is modeled by $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$. The compatible unit maps give $c=(c_n):P\to\prod_nP_n$ and $(1-s)c=0$; the comparison to this cone is the chain map $(c,0)$: explicitly write $L^i=Q^i\oplus Q^{i-1}$ with $d_L(x,y)=(d_Qx,(1-s)x-d_Qy)$, so $d_L(c(p),0)=(c(d_Pp),0)$. The displayed completeness condition requires this specified reduction comparison to be an isomorphism in the derived category, equivalently a quasi-isomorphism of these representatives. This retains the coherent reduction maps and their strict zero homotopy; it does not replace the comparison by an unrelated isomorphism between the underlying objects. The strict-augmentation clause of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] identifies $(c,0)$ with the canonical map to total derived inverse limit: it specifies the zero shifted-product component, rather than choosing an arbitrary lift of the maps in the triangulated category.

source.place: Tag 08TC, definition-derived-limit and paragraph following it; Bhatt-Scholze, Definition 3.5.2 gives the completeness convention (only the convention, not a coefficient comparison)

proof.text: The condition just defined is independent of the representative by [lem-pe-kflat-roos-representative-invariance], applied to $R\to B_n$ and the exact countable products established in the preceding step. For any other K-flat representative $P'$ with flat terms and any chosen identification $Q(P)\cong Q(P')$, that lemma supplies an isomorphism between the Roos objects commuting with the two specified augmentations. Hence one augmentation is invertible exactly when the other is. This cites the general ring-tower invariant, with its comparison of the actual maps, not merely an isomorphism of the limit objects.

proof.text: By definition, derivedStep is the unit of the consecutive scalar-extension adjunction followed by restriction of the component of reductionComp. Applying the inverse adjunction hom equivalence recovers precisely that component, by homEquiv_unit and Equiv.symm_apply_apply. A component of a natural isomorphism is invertible, proving derivedReduction_isNormalized. Compatibility of the canonical units is unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app for the composite adjunction transported by restrictComp, followed by naturality of restrictComp. proof.text: The cohomology warning is substantive. Set $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and take any nonempty $X$. The finite discrete rings $\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ give constant finite ring sheaves $B_n$: for a finite discrete set its condensed sheaf is the corresponding finite coproduct of the terminal sheaf, and geometric inverse image preserves this coproduct. By [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback] and [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact], $p_X^*$ is exact, so the finite-ring kernel computations can equally be pulled back. Take $K=[R\xrightarrow{\ell}R]$ in degrees $-1,0$. It is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site], as its two terms are free of rank one. Its reductions are therefore $[B_n\xrightarrow{\ell}B_n]$, a normalized tower by steps 6-7. Their $H^{-1}$ is the constant sheaf associated to $\ell^{n-1}\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, nonzero and isomorphic to $\mathbf F_\ell$. The transition sends the generator $\ell^n\bmod\ell^{n+1}$ to zero modulo $\ell^n$. Consequently $H^{-1}(K_{n+1})\otimes_{B_{n+1}}B_n\to H^{-1}(K_n)$ is zero between nonzero copies of the constant residue-field sheaf, and is not an isomorphism. Thus derived normalization does not assert ordinary-tensor normalization on cohomology. The only finite-ring arithmetic used is that $\ell a=0\bmod\ell^n$ exactly when $a$ is divisible by $\ell^{n-1}$.

I read every cited statement and checked the Stacks sources at their labels: 03EK, 0GMW (sites-modules.tex:3606), 06YS (sites-cohomology.tex:3207), 06YY (3585), 08TC, 0G7E and 06YQ. The coefficient ring is Layer B R=p_X^* of the condensed ring O_E, not the completed sheaf; the item is a definition, so there is no base-change morphism. Step checks: the Roos differential squares to zero; (c,0) is a chain map because (1-s)c=0; after swapping coordinates and negating one, it matches Cone(1-s)[-1] of def-weil-abstract-derived-category; and the strict-augmentation clause of lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison gives the canonical map. The step 7 balanced inverses are coherent. The step 8 counterexample holds: at ell=2, n=1 the kernel {0,2} in Z/4 goes to 0 in Z/2, so the transition-induced comparison is zero between nonzero F_ell sheaves when X is nonempty. Both new nodes are true and general, not restatements, and the DAG has no duplicate. Lemma 1: sheafification is strong monoidal, so the coequalizer is the sheafified presheaf coequalizer, and the identity-on-underlying equivalence preserves Tot, flatness and K-flatness. Lemma 2: an acyclic K-flat cone stays acyclic after tensoring with B_n; with exact products and the five lemma L(a) is a quasi-isomorphism; for a general derived isomorphism, a roof resolved K-flatly gives v. I tested edge cases (zero ring and modules, empty site, P=0, constant tower). I accept the new tool use lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison and the other 7 declared generic tools. One repaired fault (E5/C4): step 3 applied derived extension of scalars, which is defined on resolutions that are K-flat in the preserves-quasi-isomorphism sense of sk-def-sfb-derived-categories, to P, which is K-flat only in the acyclic-test sense of def-pc-kflat-complex.
